earlier_scan.source_named: Retired ISO code (xst), split 2008 into Silt'e [stv] and Wolane [wle]; no distinct documentation

new_statements.quote: Stress is conditioned by the syllabic structure: it falls on the last vowel of the word that is followed by a consonant. In other words, final closed syllables are stressed, and if the final syllable is open, the stress is penultimate. It seems, however, that sentence stress plays a more important role than word stress.
new_statements.citation: Hetzron, Robert. 1996. Notes on East Gurage. In Petr Zemánek (ed.), Studies in Near Eastern Languages and Literatures: Memorial Volume of Karel Petráček, 245-259. Prague: Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic, Oriental Institute.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress goes to the final syllable when it is closed (ends in a consonant); when the final syllable is open, stress is on the penultimate syllable. Word stress is described as weak relative to sentence stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; author hedges that sentence stress 'plays a more important role than word stress'. Data are 1965-66 field notes from one Selti, one Wolane and one Enneqor speaker, with 'no claim.. made about dialectal division'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (position stated relative to word-final syllable), with an explicit remark that phrase/sentence stress dominates. Covers the whole East Gurage dialect cluster (Selti, Wolane, Enneqor) = exactly the scope of retired ISO code [xst].
new_statements.identity_note: silt1241 is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for the retired ISO code [xst] 'Silt'e', split by ISO 639-3 change request 2007-114 (adopted 2008-02-28) into Silt'e [stv] = silt1240 and Wolane [wle] = wola1253; it has no descriptive literature of its own (Glottolog lists only the change-request PDF). The quoted statement (Hetzron 1996: 248) describes the East Gurage dialect cluster from Selti, Wolane and Enneqor speakers, i.e. the former [xst] scope; it should be filed under silt1240 (Silt'e, primary) and wola1253 (Wolane), both of which are separate targets in our source list with their own held directories, not under this retired code (a retired code does not make a separate language; counting one entity per current languoid).

sources.note: p. 248 (§2 Phonology): stress conditioned by syllable structure — falls on the last vowel followed by a consonant, i.e. final closed syllable stressed, otherwise penultimate; sentence stress said to matter more than word stress. Data from Selti (S), Wolane (W) and Enneqor (E) speakers, 1965-66; 'no claim is made about dialectal division'.
